name: Diegetic To Non-Diegetic Music Bridge
use_when: A scene has a plausible in-world source for music, such as a car, room, phone, venue, radio, or speaker.
The editor wants the track to feel motivated before it becomes full cinematic score.
A music drop would otherwise feel pasted onto the scene.
avoid_when: There is no plausible source for the track in the scene.
The source-filtered sound would confuse the viewer or distract from dialogue.
The transition to full mix would misrepresent the reality of documentary footage.
The track is unlicensed or only temp-safe.

timeline_pattern.source_rule: Establish or imply the source before applying a radio, speaker, or room filter.
timeline_pattern.opening_rule: Open the track into full bandwidth on a meaningful action, wide shot, reveal, or section shift.
timeline_pattern.duck_rule: Duck or filter the track again before important dialogue.

motion.rule: Use the visual expansion or action turn as the moment the music expands from source sound to full score.

sound.rule: Use EQ, gain, stereo width, and ambience to make the first version feel diegetic, then automate toward full-range non-diegetic music.

filter_values.radio_start: Start narrower and quieter than the full mix; reduce lows and highs, narrow stereo, and add light room/source texture.
filter_values.full_mix: Restore bandwidth, stereo width, and level at the drop while keeping dialogue ducked.
filter_values.transition: Crossfade or automate filter removal over the action turn unless a hard stylized switch is intentional.

captions.rule: Captions should not cover the action or source cue that motivates the music bridge.

color.rule: No direct color rule; keep the source context visually readable if it motivates the bridge.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use highpass, lowpass, equalizer, volume, pan, afade, and optional aecho/reverb-style processing to create a source-filtered pre-cue before opening to full mix.
implementation.remotion: Represent the bridge with sourceStartFrame, filterEndFrame, dropFrame, fullMixGain, and duckFrames.
implementation.blender: Use audio markers to synchronize the camera or scene expansion with filter removal.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Apply a radio/speaker filter at the start, then keyframe it off and raise volume/stereo feel at the drop.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Automate EQ, gain, and reverb/room tone; mark source, filter release, drop, duck, and exit.

common_mistakes: Using a radio filter without establishing why the music is in the scene.
Switching to full mix on a weak visual beat.
Leaving the filtered track too quiet or muddy to recognize the cue.
Opening to full mix and burying dialogue.
Using diegetic treatment in documentary where it falsely implies music was present.
qc: Is the in-world music source established or strongly implied?
Does the full mix open on a meaningful visual or story turn?
Does the filtered section sound intentionally sourced rather than broken?
Is dialogue clear before and after the bridge?
Is the bridge truthful for documentary footage?
